R010-01.notes: Passage describes the decoy effect, then P4-P5 weigh its real-world reach. A is only the setup; B not argued; C contradicts P3.

flags: minor: key closely paraphrases P2 ('a comparison that is easy to make... the option that wins it'), making it a lift-and-match item
minor: C is directly contradicted by 'tells them nothing new', so it is only a careless-reader trap
R010-02.notes: P2: people lean toward the winner of the easy comparison. B, D unsupported; C contradicted.

R010-03.notes: Parenthetical spells out why print-only is dominated by print-and-online. D false (online-only is cheapest); B wrong plan; A not claimed.

flags: minor: A is the observed result, a reasonable trap for students who confuse model prediction with outcome
R010-04.notes: P3: under the model, adding an unchosen option 'should not change which of the remaining options is preferred.'

R010-05.notes: The effect poses a problem for the model (a challenge, not emotional distress). A 'distressing' is the common-meaning trap; C, D off.

flags: minor: near-verbatim detail retrieval from P4
R010-06.notes: P4: 'described by many attributes, or when people already hold strong preferences.' C inverts the lab point.

flags: minor: B, C, D are all extreme ('main force', 'ever... at all', 'sure... wasting money'), so the moderate key stands out
R010-07.notes: Final sentence: whether decoys work in stores 'has not yet settled.' Author is open/undecided.

R010-08.notes: Skeptics say the effect is reliable in simple lab tasks but weak in real, many-attribute decisions; D is a real-world, many-feature null result. A is consistent with both sides (only lab); B undercuts the skeptics; C is irrelevant self-report.

flags: minor: 'Even so' makes the contrast relationship easy to spot
R010-09.notes: P5 opens 'Even so': businesses use decoys despite P4's doubts, and the question stays unsettled. B contradicted by last sentence; C overstates ('only'); D not argued.

flags: minor: A, B, D are not discussed in P3 and are easily eliminated
R010-10.notes: P3: the cells were immune cells that accumulated iron 'for unrelated reasons.' B overstates; the passage says magnetite idea is not abandoned.
